anomalies.observed: The CAN transceiver CANL pins are tied to the same net on both buses: U30 pin6 (CANL) and U35 pin6 (CANL) both carry NET0121. The two M12 CAN connectors also share the same data nets: J31 pin5/pin8 are NET0009/NET0121 and J29 pin5/pin8 are NET0009/NET0121.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires two isolated, separate CAN buses (CAN0 and CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 and isolated transceiver and broken out on its own connector. CAN0_H/CAN0_L and CAN1_H/CAN1_L should be distinct nets.

evidence.quote: U30 pin6 CANL NET0121; U35 pin6 CANL NET0121; J31 pin5 NET0009, pin8 NET0121; J29 pin5 NET0009, pin8 NET0121

two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion), broken out on M12 circular connectors `J2` ("CAN Interface A") and `J13` ("CAN Interface B")

anomalies.impact: The two CAN buses are merged at least on CANL and, as drawn on the connectors, also share the same differential net names. This defeats the intended bus isolation and would cause CAN0 and CAN1 to interfere with each other or fail to communicate correctly with the motor controllers.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows the two intended separate CAN buses sharing the same differential nets, contradicting the specification's two isolated CAN buses; this is the main anomaly.
